name: Spatial Partitioning for Parallelism

# Spatial Partitioning for Parallelism

Also called: Chunk-based Parallelism, Distributed Volume Rendering

## Overview
Spatial Partitioning for Parallelism divides a volumetric dataset into independent chunks to distribute I/O and computation across multiple processing units, solving the memory and throughput bottlenecks of large-scale volume rendering [1093-mpi-based-volume-partitioning.md][4156-object-space-decomposition-with-local-clustering.md][12593-shardedvolume.md]. It differs from tree-based methods by using fixed or pre-computed spatial divisions rather than [hierarchical traversal](#896-hierarchical-traversal.md), and from streaming methods by focusing on static or semi-static data distribution for parallel execution rather than temporal or view-dependent chunk loading [1093-mpi-based-volume-partitioning.md][2369-chunk-based-world-streaming.md].

## Shared principles
The global volume domain $\Omega$ is partitioned into a grid of chunks [G]. For a [regular grid](#3950-regular-grid.md), the chunk index $\mathbf{k} = (k_x, k_y, k_z)$ for a voxel at global coordinate $\mathbf{p} = (x, y, z)$ is calculated as:
$$
k_x = \lfloor x / W_x \rfloor, \quad k_y = \lfloor y / W_y \rfloor, \quad k_z = \lfloor z / W_z \rfloor
$$
where $W_x, W_y, W_z$ are the chunk dimensions in voxels [G]. Each chunk is treated as an independent unit for loading, processing, or rendering [G]. To prevent boundary artifacts (e.g., black stripes in [compositing](#2436-compositing.md) or discontinuities in isosurfaces) caused by naive non-overlapping division, a small overlap of data may be included among adjacent datasets [1093-mpi-based-volume-partitioning.md]. These extra/duplicated slices are used for boundary calculations but must be removed before final compositing to prevent image stretching [1093-mpi-based-volume-partitioning.md].

## Subtopics

### [MPI-based Volume Partitioning](1093-mpi-based-volume-partitioning.md)
A data-parallel strategy where a volume is divided into contiguous chunks (typically slices) assigned to distinct MPI processes. It uses a fixed, regular grid, simplifying [load balancing](#19162-load-balancing.md) for uniform data but requiring explicit boundary handling [1093-mpi-based-volume-partitioning.md].

### [Object-space decomposition with local clustering](4156-object-space-decomposition-with-local-clustering.md)
Partitions unstructured volumes into spatially coherent clusters based on topological connectivity using [graph partitioning](#4250-remapping-phase.md). It uses a view-independent preprocessing phase to build a contracted graph, allowing efficient view-dependent remapping without re-partitioning geometry [4156-object-space-decomposition-with-local-clustering.md].

### [ShardedVolume](12593-shardedvolume.md)
A data structure partitioning a 3D volume into independent shards to facilitate parallel processing and memory management. It emphasizes arithmetic operations and direct data access (e.g., slice extraction) over inter-process communication protocols [12593-shardedvolume.md].

## Background
The concept of spatial partitioning for parallel volume rendering originated with the need to scale ray-casting and [isosurface extraction](#30-isosurface-extraction.md) to datasets exceeding single-node memory. Early implementations used simple slice-based [decomposition](#7254-decomposition.md) across MPI processes [1093-mpi-based-volume-partitioning.md]. Subsequent research introduced graph-partitioning techniques for unstructured grids to minimize communication during rendering [4156-object-space-decomposition-with-local-clustering.md]. More recently, high-level abstractions like [ShardedVolume](#12593-shardedvolume.md) have been developed to manage distributed volumetric data for scientific computing and machine learning workloads [12593-shardedvolume.md].
